sources.label: Anthropic prompt-eng interactive tutorial (clear/direct/structured)
sources.summary: Canonical guidance: be clear and direct, give each instruction element one organized place, skip preamble/filler. Supports removing duplicated instruction blocks while preserving structured anchors — consistent with the enforcement-class templates already in this repo.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The repo already has a mature, code-enforced compression architecture: (1) briefing-packet consumption replaces duplicated correctness prose with generated _briefingPacket slices; (2) the Prose-Load Reduction enforcement-class model (fully/partially/inherently-prose) + Caveman-full wording layer defines HOW to compress with contract tokens frozen; (3) drift tests pin spine anchors, packet anchors, embedded-methodology markers, exact frontmatter equality, and many exact phrasings. Against this backdrop, the alternative that matches approved proposal scope (within-command repetition only) AND preserves standalone execution, sub-agent packets, approval semantics, and asset tests is a targeted within-command dedup pass classified through the existing enforcement-class templates. Concrete proof it is real and safe: adv-review.md carries the 12-dimension table twice (embedded methodology + standalone) — one canonical instance + a same-file pointer satisfies every asset assertion. Cross-command abstraction (shared includes/partials) is a genuine alternative but is out of scope per the proposal and structurally hostile to standalone-command execution: each adv-*.md must be self-contained because OpenCode loads a single command file as the prompt; extracting shared blocks would break self-containment and force a loader/runtime change the proposal excludes. Advisory line baselines confirm bloat is real (adv-apply 730 vs 404) but are warn-only, so they neither block work nor justify aggressive compression that risks contract-token or anchor loss.

validation.notes: No blockers. A within-command dedup pass is feasible and preserves all four required invariants IF it keeps every spine anchor (## Problem/## Chosen direction/## Delivered + --- + **{change-id}**), keeps briefing-packet anchors without re-adding banned manual sections, keeps inline ### *Methodology markers and skill+fallback pairs, keeps exact frontmatter=manifest equality, and freezes contract tokens. Run commands-spine-assets, briefing-packets-command-assets, adv-skill-backed-commands-assets, and manifest-doc-drift after edits. Caution (non-blocking): many exact-substring assertions pin phrasing, so mechanical caveman rewrite risks breaking them — dedup must remove duplicate INSTANCES, not reword surviving canonical text.

tradeoffs: Targeted within-command dedup keeps each command self-contained (required for standalone load) but leaves cross-command similarity uncompressed — acceptable given proposal scope and loader constraints.
Consolidating a duplicated block to one canonical instance + pointer reduces tokens but adds small same-file indirection.
Enforcement-class templates preserve safety (frozen contract tokens) at the cost of not achieving maximal raw line reduction.
Advisory-only baselines allow compression but provide no machine gate proving the dedup happened, so verification leans on exact-substring asset tests plus a manual before/after line diff.

alternatives_considered.option: Targeted within-command dedup via existing enforcement-class templates (remove duplicate instances, keep one canonical block)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Matches approved proposal scope; preserves standalone execution, packets, approval semantics, and every asset test; proven-safe example (adv-review 12-dimension table duplicated) exists.

alternatives_considered.option: Cross-command shared includes/partials (extract common blocks to a shared file)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Out of scope per proposal AND structurally breaks standalone command self-containment; OpenCode loads one command file as the prompt, so shared partials require a loader/runtime change the proposal excludes.

alternatives_considered.option: Aggressive caveman-full reword of all surviving prose
alternatives_considered.rationale: High regression risk: many asset tests assert exact substrings and frontmatter must exactly equal manifest.ts; rewording survivors (vs deleting duplicate instances) would break drift tests and could drop contract tokens.

alternatives_considered.option: Tighten advisory line baselines into a hard failing gate
alternatives_considered.rationale: Baselines are intentionally warn-only; converting to a hard gate is a separate runtime/spec change beyond within-command repetition scope and risks blocking legitimate future growth.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed with a scoped within-command dedup pass. For each large command (start adv-apply, adv-review, adv-prep, adv-discover, adv-harden), find blocks that appear twice within the same file, keep one canonical instance, replace the other with a same-file pointer, and classify surviving explanatory prose with the fully/partially/inherently-prose template. Freeze all contract tokens and delete duplicate instances rather than rewording survivors. Verify with commands-spine-assets, briefing-packets-command-assets, adv-skill-backed-commands-assets, and manifest-doc-drift tests, plus a before/after line-count diff against token-budgets.json baselines.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Do targeted within-command dedup only (proposal scope): delete duplicate block instances, keep one canonical copy + same-file pointer, freeze contract tokens, re-run the 3 command-asset tests + manifest-doc-drift. Do NOT introduce cross-command shared includes (breaks standalone load) and do NOT aggressively reword surviving text (breaks exact-substring assertions). rq- trace-tag preservation is not required — prior removeCommandTraceTags change already moved that ownership into plugin/src/ tests.
follow_ups: Confirm no command besides adv-review carries a fully duplicated table/section instance before editing (grep repeated headings per file).
After dedup, consider a separate out-of-scope change to refresh advisory line baselines in .opencode/token-budgets.json downward to reflect new sizes.

AC1: adv-review.md genuinely renders the 12-dimension framework twice (canonical Phase 0 `#### 12-Dimension Framework` at L37-56, and a redundant standalone `## 12-Dimension Review Framework` at L97-113); no test pins the later duplicate or the Sub-Agent Resilience table, so replacing the later copy with a precise same-file reference to Phase 0 is safe and loses no behavioral content (identical dimension names). AC4 protected anchors are enforced by dedicated asset tests, so the design's 'preserve unchanged' is machine-checkable (P33-aligned). AC2 compaction targets carry no exact-text pins beyond the structural anchors AC4 already protects. The design's mitigations (freeze tokens, delete duplicates rather than reword survivors, same-file references only, no cross-command include) directly counter the real risks. The change extends an existing repo compression pattern (briefing packets + asset tests) without introducing shared-include architecture, honoring C3/OOS2.

validation.notes: Design is standalone-safe and consistent with all current trunk anchors. One execution note (non-blocking): AC1 same-file reference must point at the Phase 0 `#### 12-Dimension Framework` (L37-56) as canonical owner and preserve the 'All 12 must be checked' obligation. AC3 execution outcome for the adv-apply rebase note and adv-archive T28 labels must be NO EDIT — source proof confirms both are current, not stale; editing them would violate AC3 and DONT1 (frozen contract tokens like `preExecutionRebase`, `T28*`, `detectSkipDuplicate`). Execution must re-run the targeted asset suites named in AC5 plus adv-reviewer-asset.test.ts (frontend fallback) since adv-review.md is edited.

tradeoffs: Same-file reference (vs. keeping the second full table) trades a small amount of local self-containment for reduced duplication; acceptable because Phase 0 is early in the same file and remains the single source of truth.

Retaining the live rebase/T28 markers unchanged keeps prose longer than a naive 'looks redundant, cut it' pass would, but preserves accuracy against test-backed source — correctness over brevity (P19: simplicity governs solution, not effort).

Manual per-command compaction (no shared include) keeps each command independently loadable at the cost of not eliminating cross-command boilerplate; this is a deliberate constraint (C3/OOS2), not an oversight.

alternatives_considered.option: Cross-command shared-template/include mechanism to dedupe boilerplate globally
alternatives_considered.rationale: Explicitly out of scope (OOS2) and violates C3 + the standalone-loadable requirement (SC2). Would couple command documents and break independent readability.

alternatives_considered.option: Delete the adv-apply rebase note and adv-archive T28 labels as presumed-stale
alternatives_considered.rationale: Source verification proves preExecutionRebase and all T28 symbols exist and are test-backed on trunk. Deleting/rewording would introduce documentation drift and violate AC3 + DONT1.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the second 12-dimension table verbatim (no consolidation)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Defeats AC1/SC1 goal of reducing genuine within-command duplication. A same-file reference retains all behavior with less bloat and no test breakage.

alternatives_considered.option: Reword survivor tokens/tables to 'tidy' them while consolidating
alternatives_considered.rationale: Risks breaking exact asset anchors; design correctly mandates 'delete duplicates, not reword survivors' to protect frozen contract tokens (DONT1).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to planning. documents.proposal:
# Consolidate command repetitions

## Goal
Audit current ADV command prompts and remove only proven within-command repetition while preserving phase-local contracts, worker schemas, tests, and standalone command behavior.

## Scope
- Current `.opencode/command/adv-*.md` content on trunk.
- Directly affected command-asset tests.

## Out of scope
- Cross-command abstraction, runtime/schema/spec changes, and stale `updateAgentGuide` branch recovery.

## Initial evidence
The prior `updateAgentGuide` branch is already merged and stale. This change starts from current trunk and re-audits actual command text before editing.

## Discovery Findings

### Discovery Checklist
| Step | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Skills considered | PASS | Loaded `adv-instructions-audit`; applies to command-prose claims and test anchors. |
| Prior research extension | PASS | `docs/*-prep.md` exists, but all packs concern latency, tests, slop scanning, or non-code rigor; none addresses command repetition. New finding: a literal within-command duplicate exists in `adv-review.md`. |
| Conflict scan | PASS | Active stale `updateAgentGuide` is explicitly out of scope; no active change claims this narrow audit. Own `NO_TASKS`/`NO_DELTAS` warnings are expected before prep. |
| Edge cases | PASS | Preserve embedded runtime methodology and phase-local standalone instructions; avoid deleting test-anchored cancellation/doom-loop text. |
| Design questions | PASS | One technical consolidation choice remains: canonical matrix location with a local pointer; agent-resolved toward embedded methodology ownership. |
| Draft spec deltas | PASS | No spec deltas required: current specs govern discovery/process, not this narrow document de-duplication. |
| Related-pattern scan | PASS | `adv-apply.md` contains pointers/tail recaps, but only `adv-review.md` has a proven near-identical full matrix. |
| LBP check | PASS | No external alternatives apply: internal command documentation change. Single-source-per-surface plus executable anchors is the durable direction. |
| Completeness verification | PASS | Sole-entry claim is false: do not generalize one candidate into a cross-command rewrite. Secondary candidates remain explicit dispositions. |

### Skills Considered
- `adv-instructions-audit` — loaded; requires each retained load-bearing claim to map to a fidelity anchor.
- No skill gap: this is a narrow internal command-prose audit.

### Extends
No prior research found relevant to command repetition. Existing prep packs were inspected and excluded as unrelated.

### Conflict Scan
- `updateAgentGuide` is active but the proposal explicitly excludes stale-branch recovery.
- `adv_change_validate` passed with no conflicts; its `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS` warnings are expected pre-prep state.
- Agenda has no identified item that owns this exact audit.

### Current State
- `.opencode/command/adv-review.md:37-56` embeds a 12-row review matrix as its runtime methodology.
- `.opencode/command/adv-review.md:97-111` repeats the same 12 rows in Phase 1. The only material wording loss is `OWASP top 10` in the later Security row.
- `adv-reviewer-asset.test.ts` reads the command asset but does not anchor this duplicate matrix.
- `adv-apply.md` contains related pointer/recap patterns, but its retry block, completion policy, and tail state-tool table carry phase-local or test-anchored behavior and are not proven safe to consolidate in this change.
- `adv-archive.md` has two `Step 4` labels; this is a label-collision defect, not content repetition.

### Edge Cases
1. Deleting the Phase 1 matrix without a pointer can make a standalone phase read lose the 12-dimension requirement.
2. Retaining a shortened canonical matrix can silently drop the `OWASP top 10` security scope.
3. Consolidating `adv-apply.md` retry/cancellation text can break `human-checkpoints-assets.test.ts` anchors or bury workflow-critical exits.
4. Treating the archive Step 4 label collision as duplicate prose would expand scope into release workflow sequencing.

### Open Design Questions
- **Canonical matrix location** — trust model: agent-only; blast radius: reviewer may miss a mandatory dimension if a pointer is unclear; alternatives: keep both (rejected: drift risk), retain only Phase 1 (rejected: violates embedded-methodology ownership), retain Phase 0 and add a precise Phase 1 pointer (recommended).

### Draft Spec Deltas
No spec deltas required. This change removes document-level duplication without changing durable workflow behavior or a spec law.

### Related Pattern Scan
- `adv-apply.md:72-80` and `:300-338`: retry pointer plus canonical detail — intentional canonical-reference pattern; retain.
- `adv-apply.md:715-730`: non-overlapping trivial-task and state-tool recaps; retain.
- `adv-archive.md:275,312`: rename/relabel candidate only; no content consolidation in this scope.

### Completeness Verification
- Problem completeness: supported by exact duplicate 12-row matrix evidence and a one-word security-scope divergence.
- Solution scope: bounded to one proven duplication and its direct regression anchor; no cross-command abstraction.
- Confidence: high for the review-matrix duplication; low for broader candidate removals, which are excluded.

### LBP Check
No external alternatives apply. Keep one canonical embedded matrix, preserve all twelve dimensions and security wording, and use a local Phase 1 reference. This follows command ownership while preventing duplicate drift.

### Recommended Objectives
1. Retain one canonical 12-dimension review matrix in `adv-review.md` embedded methodology.
2. Replace the repeated Phase 1 matrix with a clear local reference that preserves its mandatory-use meaning.
3. Add or update a direct asset assertion so future duplicate reintroduction or security-scope loss fails.
4. Leave `adv-apply.md` and `adv-archive.md` behavior unchanged in this change.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS
B1 LOW Boundaries — proposal says "remove only proven within-command repetition" but does not name the candidate.
  Evidence: "remove only proven within-command repetition"
  Reason: discovery resolves the candidate to the duplicated `adv-review.md` matrix and excludes adjacent patterns.
F1 LOW Functional Scope — requested preservation of "standalone command behavior" lacks a test boundary.
  Evidence: "preserving phase-local contracts, worker schemas, tests, and standalone command behavior"
  Reason: discovery adds a direct command-asset regression obligation.
S1 LOW Completion Signals — proposal names audit but not observable success.
  Evidence: "Audit current ADV command prompts"
  Reason: criteria will require one matrix, retained OWASP text, pointer, and passing direct asset test.
M1 LOW Missing Information — user preference for narrow-only versus adjacent cleanup is not stated.
  Evidence: "Current `.opencode/command/adv-*.md` content on trunk."
  Reason: resolve in the mandatory clarification round.
Coverage: B:C F:C S:C M:P

### Trigger Evaluation
Clean. No CRITICAL findings; no HIGH findings.

# Agreement — Consolidate command repetitions

## Objectives
1. Remove true same-file duplicate blocks and preserve one canonical local owner.
2. Compress standalone-safe local boilerplate without shared includes or runtime changes.
3. Correct stale command markers only after source/history proof.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1:** `adv-review.md` has one full 12-dimension framework definition; later usage is a local reference that retains required scanner behavior.
- **AC2:** Target-resolution, skill-wrapper, worktree-context, auto-continue, and sub-agent-context prose are compacted only where command-specific behavior and frozen contract tokens remain explicit.
- **AC3:** `adv-apply` rebase wording and `adv-archive` T28 labels change only when source/history confirms they are stale; otherwise they remain unchanged.
- **AC4:** Gate Handoff, approval, briefing-packet, embedded-methodology, and frontend-fallback anchors remain intact.
- **AC5:** Targeted command asset tests and `pnpm run check` exit 0.

## Success Criteria
- **SC1:** Current command bloat is reduced without cross-command include architecture.
- **SC2:** Each changed command remains independently readable and behaviorally complete.

## Constraints
- No runtime, schema, spec, tool, or agent behavior changes.
- Token budgets remain advisory.
- No cross-command shared-template/include mechanism.

## Avoidances
- Do not reword frozen contract tokens merely to reduce prose.
- Do not delete phase-local worker schemas or test-pinned fallback content.

## Out of Scope
- Hard token-budget enforcement.
- Shared command loader/include architecture.
- Recovery of stale `updateAgentGuide` work.

## Approval Evidence
User approved safe local cleanup, source-backed stale-marker correction, advisory-only budgets, and this agreement on 2026-07-13.

# Design — Consolidate command repetitions

## Architecture
Keep every ADV command independently loadable. Remove only duplicated instances within a command or shorten local explanatory wrappers. Never replace content with cross-command pointers or include mechanisms.

## Implementation Strategy
1. Inventory every targeted candidate before editing; classify frozen contract tokens and protected anchors.
2. In `adv-review`, retain the Phase 0 12-dimension table and replace the later full duplicate with a precise same-file reference before the distinct Phase 2 scanner contract.
3. Compact safe local wrapper prose for target resolution, skill loading, worktree propagation, auto-continue, and sub-agent context only when their per-command behavior remains explicit.
4. Verify `adv-apply` rebase wording against actual pre-rebase call sites and `adv-archive` T28 labels against reachable source/history. Correct only proven stale text.
5. Preserve Gate Handoff spine, inline approval text, briefing packet anchors, embedded methodology markers, and frontend fallback unchanged.

## Verification
- Deterministic before/after inventory and line diff.
- Targeted command-asset suites: spine, briefing packet, skill-backed commands, manifest drift, review/archive/apply assets.
- `pnpm run check`.

## Risks
- Local shortening can erase a command-specific condition. Mitigation: freeze tokens and use same-file references only.
- Stale-looking text may describe intentionally deferred behavior. Mitigation: require source/history evidence before edit.
- Exact asset anchors can break on rewrites. Mitigation: delete duplicates, not reword survivors.

## LBP
The repository already uses briefing packets and asset tests as structural compression mechanisms. This change extends that pattern only inside individual command documents.
